scope: Reuse existing grouped contributor plans in all three histogram consumers; numerical, storage, ownership, API/ABI and default-cap contracts unchanged.
implementation: Histogram vector arguments seed transient demand on the accounted roster-task stack, independently of outer wrappers.
Ordinary aggregates and existing supported maps propagate demand; scalar/string arguments, unsupported edges and changed clocks keep fallback evaluation.
Existing selector/grid proofs, output ordinals, successful complete-child credit, exact keys, fresh selected values and preparation clearing remain authoritative.
Pair-only Float/cardinality restrictions stay with joins. No new raw-value cache or persistent context array is added.

controls.phase_proof: Drive the histogram call body directly, check completion, then calibrate subsequent acquisitions. API output-head buffering is tested separately from evaluator phases.
controls.cold_warm_interruption_and_release: Both optimized rosters cover all three functions, page sizes and independent name modes.
controls.c_basic_statistics: Logical totals, useful reads and actual sample peaks are observed through C; all logical totals remain exact.

memory.scope: Reader over completed bound query executions; no new engine execution or timing claim.

timing.scope: Five measured alternating native-release pairs after one warmup pair. Shared host, finite synthetic provider. Complete analytical/retained outcomes and every nonelapsed observation checked. No live/cardinality/concurrency/RSS or release-min speedup claim.

foreign_production_identical_precursor.change_scope: Only the cfg(test) module in execution.rs. Production prefix and all other frozen inputs are byte-identical. Foreign binaries retain their original full source identity; they are not reattributed to the later test source.

source_attribution.foreign_scope: Installed ARM32/ARM64 release under QEMU. Full precursor source identity is retained; a later correction changes only the excluded Rust test module. No foreign release-min, foreign Rust-unit or physical-device timing claim.

limits: Finite complete outcomes are evidence, not proof for every possible input or 100% compatibility.
Five measured alternating native-release pairs on a shared host; no CPU/frequency isolation or maximum-throughput claim.
Peak tracked workspace can increase for membership metadata; lower allocation traffic does not prove lower RAM/RSS.
Synthetic provider timings and unchanged real API regressions are separate; no live speedup or high-cardinality/cold-disk claim.
Ordered range consumers still repeat some All discovery. The multi-tick controls retain its measured residual cost.
Raw source histories remain paged; provider temporary-backing and disabled-cap policies are unchanged.
